references.text: The background to the Midianites' oppression of Israel, from which Gideon later delivered them
Gideon's victory over the Midianites, where he risked his life to deliver Israel
After the victory over Midian, Gideon refused to become king over Israel
Midian was humbled and the land had peace for forty years during Gideon's time
Abimelech, Gideon's son, seized power by killing his brothers—in contrast to his father's self-sacrifice
The psalm recalls the victory over Midian and their leaders as an example of God's mighty deliverance
Isaiah refers to 'the day of Midian' as a picture of God's deliverance
